objective: Replace competing physical-unit representations across geometry, meshing, analysis, solver boundaries, artifacts, transport, desktop and agent context with one shared typed contract and explicit provenance.
principles: One shared unit/quantity implementation in dependency-neutral runmat-types; stable semantic aliases/reexports resolve to that implementation and are not parallel authorities.
Reuse PhysicalDimension as dimension algebra; retain distinct physical quantity kinds when dimensions coincide.
Treat source declaration, user interpretation, kernel coordinates, canonical analysis coordinates and presentation preference as different typed roles.
Unknown, conflicting and mixed file declarations are explicit states; an import default is never reported as file evidence.
One canonical numeric storage convention at each declared computation boundary; retain original source unit and value separately.
Raw numeric arrays are permitted only through typed fields/operators with checked quantity, coordinate-space and mixed-DOF layout contracts.
Codemods implement reviewed mappings. They never infer dimensions from names or silently classify unreviewed floats as dimensionless.
Each migration slice changes producer, transport, consumer, tests and generated schemas together, then removes the old authority.

target_contract.dimension: Existing PhysicalDimension algebra for products, quotients and powers.
target_contract.quantity_kind: Named semantic quantity markers; examples include Length, Displacement, Temperature, TemperatureDifference, Force, Moment, Energy, Power, ElectricCurrent and ElectricPotential.
target_contract.quantity: Quantity<Q> with private canonical value, explicit checked external construction and canonical extraction restricted to audited numeric boundaries. Vectors/fields preserve Q and shape/layout.
target_contract.unit_definition: Unit<Q> with validated scale/offset and source symbol; affine temperature conversion and temperature differences remain distinct. Runtime unit expressions are dimension/kind checked before constructing typed units.
target_contract.source_measure: SourceMeasure<Q> preserves source value, unit definition and source attribution alongside the normalized quantity.
target_contract.geometry_units: Typed length-unit evidence per representation context, plus an explicit interpretation/override and separate kernel/preview coordinate scales. Conversion metadata travels with every representation.
target_contract.field_operator: Typed Field<Q, Storage> for homogeneous quantities; explicit checked DOF/block layouts for heterogeneous systems and their operators.
target_contract.serialization: Versioned semantic contracts generated for Rust/TypeScript. Validate dimensions, finite positive scales, permitted offsets, shape and provenance at external boundaries.
target_contract.arithmetic: Typed operations for supported quantity relationships generated from the shared catalog; explicit semantic operations where dimensions alone cannot distinguish results.

acceptance: No unclassified production candidate or unmapped old representation remains within the agreed physics pipeline scope.
Wrong quantity kinds, source/kernel scale substitutions and wrong typed solver field wiring fail compilation.
All admitted external payloads pass checked construction; unknown or conflicting geometry units cannot become confirmed units silently.
Equivalent geometry expressed in mm, m and inches has equivalent physical bounds, loads and qualified solve results.
Unit provenance survives native/browser imports, serialization, artifacts, summaries and agent context.
Thermal flux/density/rate and electrical current/density/charge remain distinct; coupling conversions check measure dimensions.
Absolute temperature, temperature differences, torque/energy, angles and dimensionless scalars retain required semantic distinctions.
Dimension-changing output reductions and mixed-DOF operators carry correct result/boundary contracts.
No per-element unit metadata or avoidable allocation is introduced into numeric buffers; benchmark approved boundaries.
Relevant Rust/workspace checks, compile-fail tests, roundtrip tests, physics qualification and generated TS checks pass.
